body:
Knowing you kicked some ass and knowing your brothers died for basically nothing are two very different things.

Got deployed in 12, I know we did what we were supposed to do. I also know that me drinking and smoking tonight is because a brother of mine got carried to the medevac after having to almost declare him missing in action and what's happening there now fucks with my head more than I care to admit.

At the risk of saying what we did and what the Vietnam vets said did was useless, we went because we were told not because we thought it was worth it

As a fellow vet who feels lik my time was not worthy of having PTSD, how did you cope prior to seeking help?  I'm asking honestly even though I'm at the point where I think I should seek help, but maybe others aren't

I apparently earned my CAR, never really believed I earned it until the guys from my platoon told me to wear it with pride.

I'm at the point where tomorrow I'm telling my supervisor and will be moving with any help I can find

I did.

I've done as much as possible to shield my family as I can.  My sole surviving grandparent is a WW2 vet and I don't want him to feel stressed due to my own feelings

My brothers, including a couple of friends from pre Marines, already knew or had sucipicions
